doc.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998

title: Agents and animosity
summary: She discusses animosity directed at her and why agents are in an untenable position and bend the truth.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well said. Did you run into various degrees of honesty and dishonesty in agents in booking him in different parts?

I ran into a lot of animosity, I should say that, because people are jealous and deeply threatened and particularly because Bob is a Piscean and he’s a very gentle man, and people couldn’t understand why he was suddenly getting so taciturn and hard-nosed you know. And a lot of the time it was his idea, but it was me that was probably blamed. And as far as that was concerned I suppose it made us closer together, which was wonderful. As far as agents are concerned, I think that agents are in a very untenable position. I think they have to be dishonest even though it’s not their nature, because if they were to tell you that they don’t have any work, you’d go somewhere else. You parallel it to a builder that comes to your house. If he gives you a price that it’s really going to cost, you’re going to say I’m sorry I can’t afford it and you’ll send him on his way. If he tells you it’s going to cost less, and tells you little fibs, little fibs or big fibs, you will give him the job and then he can’t do it, and so on and so forth. It’s an untenable situation, Monk, and it’s one that happens all the time. I don’t put it down to dishonesty. I put it down to the fact that it’s an overcrowded profession. Not necessarily overcrowded with talented people. I think there’s a lot of untalented people who are getting work but that’s another issue, that’s not what I’m interested in. The fact is, there’s only so much work. And for agents, they can only provide you with so many gigs. So they might just string you along, not because they’re being devious, but because they are having to sort of say everything nice to everybody.
